_comment: Right Path MY WORK ordering decision. Adapted from IPF (bobpfromm/ipf-stewardship) src/rules/next-best-action.json — the established GoRules ZEN decision layer that owns ALL priority judgment. This decision classifies ONE activity group (a business activity the signed-in employee may act on) into a priority BAND, given independent presence facts the composition supplies. ZEN owns the ordering between bands; TypeScript owns normalization and never ranks. The ordering reflects ONLY established Right Path decisions and invents none: (a) a DUE customer commitment (a promised callback that has come due) outranks focus-based ordering — Today's Focus influences priority but never overrides a customer commitment; (b) within focus, management direction elevates ELIGIBLE work the employee can actually perform (focus never grants eligibility it lacks); (c) owned/claimed eligible work the employee committed to comes before unclaimed shared work; (d) unclaimed shared work the employee is eligible for is ordinary pickup work; (e) work the employee is NOT eligible for is visible but ranked last (shown for awareness, never routed to them). Focus NEVER disables a band — it only reorders — so ineligible and non-focus work still appear.

inputs.name: Employee is eligible for this activity

rules._description: A due customer commitment outranks everything, including Today's Focus. A promised callback that has come due is a commitment to the customer; focus influences ordering but never overrides it. Surfaced only for activities the employee is eligible to act on.
Focus-elevated AND eligible: management has directed attention here and the employee can actually perform it. Focus elevates only eligible work; it never grants eligibility.
Owned (claimed) eligible work the employee committed to, when not elevated by focus. Comes before unclaimed shared work.
Unclaimed shared work the employee is eligible for: ordinary pickup work, shared by default.
Work the employee is NOT eligible for. Visible for awareness (the activity still exists and matters), but ranked last and never routed to this employee.
